cases.sentence: Это дело не мое личное, а тут вопрос об ___.
cases.explain: «общем благе» — after the preposition «об», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I have only to go stubbornly on towards my aim, and I shall attain my end,” thought Levin; “and it’s something to work and take trouble for. This is not a matter of myself individually; the question of the public welfare comes into it. The whole system of culture, the chief element in the condition of the people, must be completely transformed. Instead of poverty, general prosperity and content; instead of hostility, harmony and unity of interests. In short, a bloodless revolution, but a revolution of the greatest magnitude, beginning in the little circle of our district, then the province, then Russia, the whole world. Because a just idea cannot but be fruitful. Yes, it’s an aim worth working for. And its being me, Kostya Levin, who went to a ball in a black tie, and was refused by the Shtcherbatskaya girl, and who was intrinsically such a pitiful, worthless creature—that proves nothing; I feel sure Franklin felt just as worthless, and he too had no faith in himself, thinking of himself as a whole. That means nothing. And he too, most likely, had an Agafea Mihalovna to whom he confided his secrets.”

cases.sentence: Пообедав, Левин сел, как и обыкновенно, с книгой на кресло и, читая, продолжал думать о своей ___ в связи с книгою.
cases.explain: «предстоящей поездке» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: After dinner Levin was sitting, as he usually did, in an easy chair with a book, and as he read he went on thinking of the journey before him in connection with his book. Today all the significance of his book rose before him with special distinctness, and whole periods ranged themselves in his mind in illustration of his theories. “I must write that down,” he thought. “That ought to form a brief introduction, which I thought unnecessary before.” He got up to go to his writing-table, and Laska, lying at his feet, got up too, stretching and looking at him as though to inquire where to go. But he had not time to write it down, for the head peasants had come round, and Levin went out into the hall to them.

cases.sentence: После наряда, то есть распоряжений по работам ___, и приема всех мужиков, имевших до него дела, Левин пошел в кабинет и сел за работу.
cases.explain: «завтрашнего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After his levee, that is to say, giving directions about the labors of the next day, and seeing all the peasants who had business with him, Levin went back to his study and sat down to work. Laska lay under the table; Agafea Mihalovna settled herself in her place with her stocking.

cases.sentence: Агафья Михайловна знала все подробности ___ Левина.
cases.explain: «хозяйственных планов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Agafea Mihalovna knew every detail of Levin’s plans for his land. Levin often put his views before her in all their complexity, and not uncommonly he argued with her and did not agree with her comments. But on this occasion she entirely misinterpreted what he had said.

cases.sentence: В девять часов послышался колокольчик и ___ кузова по грязи.
cases.explain: «глухое колебание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: At nine o’clock they heard the bell and the faint vibration of a carriage over the mud.
